content:
incident-bot: 🚨 Elevated 5xx rate detected for inference-gateway-eu-south (eu-south1). 504 spike from 1.2% -> 6.8% in last 5m. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Paging oncall: @maria, @leo. Tags: latency, gateway, region-eu-south

maria: ack. I'm taking primary. Pulling gateway and edge-proxy logs now.

leo: I see increased TCP connect times to redis-cache-eusouth and a lot of upstream ECONNRESETs in the gateway logs. Past 7m: connection attempts timing out during TLS handshake.

sam: any deploys in last 30m?

eng-oncall-bot: no deploys flagged in prod in the last 60m.

maria: pasting filtered logs from gateway (connections failing to backend):
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:13Z] gateway-eu-1 -> backend redis-cache-eusouth: dial tcp 10.4.22.18:6379: i/o timeout
[2026-03-15T10:02:14Z] gateway-eu-1 upstream: TLS handshake timeout after 30s to 10.4.22.18
[2026-03-15T10:02:15Z] gateway-eu-2 -> backend redis-cache-eusouth: connection reset by peer
```

maria: traceroute to redis-cache-eusouth shows inconsistent DNS answers from internal resolver (different pod IPs alternating, some are from decommissioned pool).

leo: that smells like stale SRV/A cache in the internal DNS or an endpoint controller flapping. If traffic is being routed to drained hosts we’ll see handshake timeouts -> gateway returns 504.

ashley: customer-impact: CS reports multiple support chats with slow responses and failover errors. Top two paying customers saw 10-15% of their requests erroring in last 20m.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily steer traffic off eu-south to eu-west for critical routes (canary 20% -> 50% if stable), 2) flush internal DNS caches on gateway hosts, 3) remove drained endpoints from service discovery, 4) monitor. Executing step 1 now.

leo: command to steer (infra run):
```
infractl traffic steer --from inference-gateway-eu-south --to inference-gateway-eu-west --routes /v1/generate,/v1/chat --percent 20 --reason "eu-south backend dns/drain errors"
```

maria: running infractl...

incident-bot: change applied: 20% traffic steered to inference-gateway-eu-west for specified routes.

leo: flushing DNS caches on gateways (systemd-resolved) and restarting sidecar resolver on gateway pods:
```
kubectl -n proxy get pods -l app=gateway -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl exec -n proxy -- bash -c 'systemd-resolve --flush-caches || kill -HUP 1'
```

sam: removing endpoints from service discovery for the drained pool (mark as out-of-service)

ashley: CS: notifying affected customers that we have a mitigaton in progress; advising degraded but improving performance.

maria: after initial 20% shift: errors dropped to 3.1% in eu-south, overall infra error rate now 1.0%. Increasing steer to 45% to reduce customer impact while we fix the root cause.

leo: increased to 45%. Observability: request latencies to eu-west rose ~40ms but within SLO. No errors in eu-west.

eng-oncall-bot: alert suppressed for inference-gateway-eu-south 504 spike (auto-mitigation in progress).

maria: root cause hypothesis: internal DNS / endpoint-controller race caused service endpoints to temporarily contain IPs of drained/decommissioned hosts. Those hosts were still advertised to the gateway DNS cache leading to intermittent handshake/connect timeouts and 504s.

sam: action items (assigned):
- sam: follow up with k8s endpoint-controller team to find why endpoints were not reconciled (ticket created).
- leo: validate sidecar resolver's cache behavior and add TTL-reload on endpoint changes.
- maria: write customer-impact summary and SRE mitigation runbook update.
- ashley (CS): run template communication for affected customers and log support cases.

ashley: CS notes sent to impacted customers; will post a consolidated update once stable.

maria: traffic is stable for 12m after 45% steer. error rate eu-south down to 0.7% and overall generation errors 0.6%. Initiating gradual rollback of steer (reduce steer by 10% every 3m) while we ensure endpoints are clean.

leo: after flushing caches and removing drained endpoints, endpoint list now stable. Rolling back steer to 0% over next 9 minutes.

incident-bot: traffic steer removed; all routes back to normal routing. Final error rate steady at 0.4%.

ashley: CS update posted: mitigated; continuing monitoring; offer to affected customers for 1:1 follow-up.

maria: creating incident report ticket and scheduling postmortem for tomorrow. TAGS: incident-sev-2, gateway, dns, failover, cs-impact.

sam: noting potential followups: add automated endpoint-change trigger to flush gateway cache + improve health-check handshake timeouts.

leo: thumbs up. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

maria: closing thread. I'll update the incident doc with timelines and metrics.
